headline: Friday's US real-rate squeeze got exported overnight — Taiwan -6.0%, Korea -3.6% — and for the first time in this drawdown the vol complex is actually paying up, with VIX +7.8% to 20.81.
summary: What changed since Friday: the pain left the US. Taiwan's TAIEX -6.0% in a session (z=-2.46, acceleration -1.84), KOSPI -3.6% and now 22.5% below its 200-day after -10.0% on the month, Nikkei -2.4% and -8.7% on the month. This is the same discount-rate trade — SMH -13.8% on the month, NVDA -26.4% and pinned at the 0th percentile of its year, SOXX -13.8% — but it is now being liquidated in the places that own the supply chain, and the US-listed proxies (EWT -12.2% 1m, EWY -10.7%) have not marked it. The difference versus yesterday is hedging: VIX 20.81 (+7.8%), VIX3M +9.7% on the month, the VIX/VIX3M term structure at 0.936 and turning up, MOVE 98.79 after +42% in three months. Last week the market rotated; today it is paying for protection.

What still refuses to confirm the panic is credit and breadth. HY OAS 3.20 (-10bp), CCC -16bp to 13.14 after +47bp on the month, IG 0.89, BKLN at the 97th percentile, HYG/IEF +1.6% on the week. RSP/SPY sits at z=3.11 with acceleration 2.83, equal-weight +4.3% on the month, Dow Transports +3.9%. And the leadership is defensive-but-rising, not cash: XLP at the 100th percentile of its year (+7.3% 1m), XLV z=1.94 with +10.8% relative strength, SPLV z=1.95, USMV 97th percentile, LLY +19.6% on the month. The economy underwriting it is intact — claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), capacity utilisation at the 100th percentile, growth pulse +3. This is still dispersion, not de-risking, but the margin is thinner: bank reserves -2.3% on the month and NFCI tightening (z=0.31).

The metals tape is where the growth message is clearest, and it is not good. Silver -3.6% today, -17.1% on the month, 30.7% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile; platinum -2.0% and -10.1%; gold -7.3% on the month and also 0th percentile. Gold/silver +3.4% today to 81.99, z=1.72 and at the 100th percentile — what is breaking is industrial demand, not the monetary bid. Copper -7.4% on the month, COPX -14.3%, FCX -14.7%, XME -6.1%, and the electrification/AI-capex complex with it: CAT -19.7% on the month at z=-2.28, ETN -13.4%, GEV -14.7%, GRID -8.1%. Meanwhile WTI -13.5% on the month and gasoline -21.1% are why breakevens sit at 2.24 (19th percentile) and 2.30 (25th). The inflation composite at +29 is a backward look at core CPI (z=0.93, turning up); the forward market is pricing disinflation plus a hawkish Fed — 10y 5.10, real 10y 2.86 and 27.5% above its 200-day, 2s10s 27bp at the 13th percentile. That is a bear-flattening hike discount, and duration-heavy cash flows keep paying for it.

FX is the transmission mechanism and it is getting more violent, not less. USDBRL +1.5% to 5.7259, +12.3% on the month, z=3.5 with acceleration 2.58 — the most extreme reading on the board, and re-accelerating even after EWZ bounced +1.4% on Friday. DXY 103.46 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.1013 at the 0th, USDCHF and USDCAD both at the 100th, AUD/JPY -1.0% and rolling over, CEW -1.0% on the month. But EM is not one trade: India's Sensex is z=2.31 with INDA +9.4% on the month and +11.6% relative strength, Mexico's IPC +6.6%, while Korea, Taiwan, Brazil and Argentina (-15.2% 1m) are in outright drawdown. Own the dispersion, own the low-vol and cash-flow-now side, and fund it in the semiconductor and crypto complex — BTC 64,313 (-21.0% 1m), ETH -24.9%, SOL -31.2%, COIN at the 0th percentile.
Credit refused to break into a global equity air pocket: HY OAS -10bp to 3.20, CCC -16bp to 13.14 after a +47bp month, IG 0.89, BKLN at the 97th percentile of its year.

good.text: Credit refused to confirm the equity break: HY OAS -10bp to 3.20, CCC -16bp to 13.14 after +47bp on the month, IG 0.89, BKLN at the 97th percentile and HYG/IEF +1.6% on the week.
Breadth is still widening against a falling index — RSP/SPY z=3.11 with acceleration 2.83, equal-weight +4.3% on the month at the 95th percentile, Dow Transports +3.9%, IYT/SPY z=2.18.
The macro underneath is not cracking: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), capacity utilisation 76.85 at the 100th percentile, retail sales +4.2% ytd.
Defensive leadership is rising, not just relatively outperforming: XLP at the 100th percentile, XLV z=1.94 (+10.8% rel 1m), SPLV z=1.95, USMV 97th percentile, LLY +19.6% on the month.
Inflation expectations keep deflating — 10y breakeven 2.24 at the 19th percentile, 5y 2.30, gasoline -21.1% and WTI -13.5% on the month — which caps how long a hike scare can run.
Europe, India and Mexico are quietly compounding: DAX at the 99th percentile (+4.3% 1m), CAC z=1.13, Sensex z=2.31, INDA +9.4% 1m, Mexico IPC +6.6%.

bad.text: Asia capitulated on the semi trade: Taiwan -6.0% (z=-2.46, acc -1.84), Korea -3.6% and 22.5% below its 200-day, Nikkei -2.4%; US proxies EWT and EWY have not marked it yet.
Hedging demand finally bid, and it is accelerating the wrong way: VIX +7.8% to 20.81, VIX3M +9.7% on the month, term structure 0.936 turning up, MOVE 98.79 after +42% in three months.
The squeeze is real, not inflationary: 10y 5.10, 10y real 2.86 and 27.5% above its 200-day, 2s10s 27bp at the 13th percentile — a bear flattening that discounts another hike.
The dollar is still breaking EM carry and USDBRL is re-accelerating: +1.5% today to 5.7259, +12.3% on the month, z=3.5 with acceleration 2.58; DXY, USDCHF and USDCAD all at the 100th percentile.
Industrial metals and the electrification/AI-capex complex are in a synchronised downtrend: copper -7.4% 1m, COPX -14.3%, FCX -14.7%, CAT -19.7% (z=-2.28), ETN -13.4%, GEV -14.7%.
Crypto keeps leaking with no stabilisation: BTC -21.0% on the month, ETH -24.9%, SOL -31.2%, IBIT -15.8%, COIN at the 0th percentile of its year.

trades.name: Long gold vs short silver
trades.line: Long gold / short silver: the industrial leg is the one breaking
trades.expr: Buy GLD against an equal-dollar short in silver futures (or SLV); gold/silver ratio long at 81.99.
trades.thesis: Both metals are being crushed by a 2.86% real 10-year, but silver is also carrying the industrial demand shock visible in copper -7.4% and COPX -14.3% on the month. The ratio is the clean way to own metal downside without fighting a possible rate-driven bounce in bullion.
trades.trigger: Silver -3.6% today and -17.1% on the month, 30.7% below its 200-day; gold/silver +3.4% to 81.99 at z=1.72 and the 100th percentile of its year, with copper also rolling over.
trades.stop: Gold/silver back below 76 — i.e. copper stabilises above 6.20 and the industrial bid returns, or a liquidity event makes gold the funding source instead.

trades.name: Low vol over high beta
trades.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB as vol finally bids
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long SPLV against short SPHB; add a December SPY put spread if you want convexity on the VIX move.
trades.thesis: A 5.10% 10-year inside a healthy economy produces rotation, not liquidation, and the rotation is mechanical: cash-flow-now beats duration. Low vol is at the 99th percentile and high beta is 3.1% below its 200-day with high-beta/low-vol at z=-2.15 and still accelerating down.
trades.trigger: VIX +7.8% to 20.81 with the term structure at 0.936 and turning up; SPHB/SPLV -13.6% on the month (acc z=-1.54) while SPLV posts z=1.95 and USMV sits at the 97th percentile.
trades.stop: Pair -4%, which would require VIX back under 17 and SMH/SPY turning up from z=-2.02.
trades.target: +6% on the pair as the ratio retraces toward its 200-day.

trades.name: India over Korea
trades.line: Long INDA / short EWY: EM is two trades, not one
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long INDA against short EWY.
trades.thesis: EM dispersion is extreme and tracks semiconductor beta and dollar funding. India is an oil importer with falling crude (-13.5% 1m), a stable rupee (USDINR -0.6% 1m) and the strongest momentum on the board; Korea is a levered long on the memory/AI cycle that is now unwinding in cash markets.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -3.6% today, -10.0% on the month and 22.5% below its 200-day; Sensex z=2.31 with acceleration 1.64, INDA +9.4% on the month and +11.6% relative strength while EWY is -8.9% relative.
trades.stop: Pair -6%; a decisive semi re-acceleration (SOXX reclaiming its 200-day, MU/AVGO follow-through) invalidates the short leg.

trades.name: Financials funded by tech
trades.line: Long XLF / short XLK on hike repricing
trades.expr: Long XLF against an equal-dollar short XLK; express the upside tail with XLF January calls if you prefer defined risk.
trades.thesis: If the December debate is a hike rather than a cut, banks and insurers are the only sector whose earnings improve with the shock, while XLK is pure duration. Insurance and brokers confirm: KIE z=1.53 with acceleration 1.65, IAI acceleration 1.34.
trades.trigger: XLF +0.8% Friday at z=1.28 (acc 1.55), 96th percentile, +9.8% relative strength on the month; XLK -10.6% on the month with -8.8% relative and rolling over; 3m10y steepened 5bp.
trades.stop: Pair -5%, or XLF relative strength rolling under its 200-day as 2-year yields fall more than 30bp from 4.86.

trades.name: Short the real
trades.line: Long USDBRL, short EWZ: the carry unwind is accelerating
trades.expr: Long USDBRL spot/forward (weight 1) with a half-size short in EWZ as the equity expression of the same funding stress.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the epicentre of the dollar squeeze: a 3.5 standard-deviation monthly FX move with acceleration still positive is not a move that ends on its own, and local equity has already repriced -24.4% in dollars. Dollar at the 100th percentile with EM FX basket -1.0% means the pressure is systemic, not idiosyncratic.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +1.5% today to 5.7259, +12.3% on the month, z=3.5 and acceleration 2.58 — the most extreme print on the board, re-accelerating even after EWZ bounced +1.4%.
trades.stop: USDBRL back under 5.50 (pair -4%) — central bank intervention or a DXY break below 102 ends it.
trades.target: USDBRL 6.05, about +6% on the combined position.

trades.name: Short crypto equity duration
trades.line: Short MSTR/COIN: zero-coupon assets vs a 2.86% real yield
trades.expr: Short MSTR and COIN in equal weight, or buy January puts on MSTR to cap the squeeze risk.
trades.thesis: Crypto equities are the most levered expression of the real-rate squeeze and they keep making new lows while the index holds up. No stabilisation signal yet: every bounce in the last month has been sold within days.
trades.trigger: BTC -1.5% today to 64,313 and -21.0% on the month, ETH -24.9%, SOL -31.2%; MSTR -22.1% on the month and 16.1% below its 200-day, COIN -26.2% and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: BTC reclaiming 72,000 or the combined short losing 12%.
trades.target: +18% on the short as BTC tests the 58-60k area.

trades.name: Fade the housing relief rally
trades.line: Short ITB vs long SPY: mortgage relief is about to reverse
trades.expr: Short ITB against an equal-dollar long SPY.
trades.thesis: Homebuilders have rallied on a lagging weekly mortgage print while the actual funding curve has moved against them. The 30-year mortgage follows the 10-year with a lag, and the 10-year is +26bp on the week. The relative move is 2 standard deviations stretched into real housing data that is deteriorating.
trades.trigger: ITB +12.7% and XHB +9.9% on the month with XHB/SPY at z=2.22 and ITB already rolling over (-2.6% on the week), against 10y 5.10, 30y 5.43 and housing starts -5.2% with permits -0.4%.
trades.stop: Pair -5%; a decisive 10-year break back under 4.80 would validate the mortgage move and the homebuilder bid.
trades.target: +7% on the pair as XHB/SPY mean-reverts toward its 200-day (-5.7% away).
